questions.question: What does `import "server-only"` at the top of a data access module do?
options: It makes the module run on the Edge runtime
It caches the module's results across requests
It causes a build error if the module is imported into a Client Component
It marks every exported function as a Server Action
questions.explanation: server-only is a guard: importing the module from client code fails the build, so database clients and secrets cannot leak into the browser bundle.

questions.question: What is the scope of memoization when you wrap an ORM query in React's `cache()`?
options: A single server request; nothing is shared between requests or users
All requests until the server restarts
questions.explanation: React cache() dedupes calls within one request, so a layout and page calling getCurrentUser() hit the database once. Cross-request caching needs a different tool such as "use cache".

questions.question: Why do serverless deployments often exhaust Postgres connections, and what is the usual fix?
options: Serverless functions cannot use TCP; switch to a REST API
Each concurrent function instance opens its own connections; route them through a pooler such as PgBouncer and keep per-instance pools small
Postgres does not support serverless; use MongoDB
React Server Components keep connections open forever; disable streaming
questions.explanation: Many short-lived instances each opening a pool quickly hit the database's connection limit. A pooler multiplexes them onto a small number of real connections.

questions.question: A page awaits three independent queries taking 120ms, 150ms and 90ms one after another. Roughly how long does it take with `Promise.all` instead?
options: About 150ms, the duration of the slowest query
questions.explanation: Sequential awaits add up (360ms). Starting them together with Promise.all means the total is bounded by the slowest one.
